llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is most consistent with a node-level optical failure at the common ROADM S20 around t=602.5 s. A WSS input-port failure is the closest documented mode, although the simultaneous OSC loss on multiple S20-facing links suggests a broader S20 site/ROADM outage not explicitly listed.

proposals.rationale: Every affected working path depends on ROADM S20, and simultaneous OCH loss across many lightpaths is consistent with channels being blocked there. The multi-degree OSC losses are broader than the stated effect of one WSS input-port failure, so a node-wide condition remains possible.

A disconnected OMS input could produce all-channel loss toward the S20-S01 amplifier chain and the observed AMP_INPUT_LOS. It cannot by itself explain the simultaneous S20-S13 and opposite-direction losses.
A disconnected OMS input could explain the all-channel loss toward S20-S13. The concurrent failures on the S20-S01 side and reverse directions argue strongly against this being the sole cause.

Large added loss on the span upstream of O1 could explain AMP_INPUT_LOS and OSC_LOS on that section. Independent simultaneous symptoms on several other S20-adjacent sections make a single-span fault unlikely.
A switch failure at the common site could interrupt many ODUs at once. However, it would not explain the widespread OCH and OSC loss alarms, which point to the optical layer.
